citations.assessment: The baraita assigns two hairs to its opening account, with the age of vows specified by R. Yosi. The youth’s conditional vow, kiss and prompt ruling are in the following segment. Heilprin recounts the age-of-vows branch.

The end of the chapter distinguishes Shimon ben Gamliel who examines from Rabban Gamliel who kisses, and includes the Yavneh testimony. The retrieved patronymic is ben Chanina, while this Heilprin witness reads ben Chananyah.

evidence.witness: The Jerusalem Talmud, edition by Heinrich W. Guggenheimer. Berlin, De Gruyter, 1999-2015

citations.assessment: The chapter names Chanina ben Chanina and says his father brought him to Rabban Gamliel. It likewise keeps physical signs and age of vows in distinct attributed versions.

holds.reason: The Yerushalmi and Tosefta digital witnesses have ben Chanina. Retain the received ben Chananyah pending printed collation.

notes.text: The three complete narratives distinguish the physical signs and age-of-vows versions, the names of examiners, and Elazar ben Tzadok’s testimony.
